releases.title: Bots that sound like a person

items.text: Everyday replies come as one to three short messages that open with the result, with no narrated plan.
Bots read the room: clean sentences for polished people, short and warm for everyone else, and they play along with a joke once.
An app you connect or reconnect mid-chat works on the next message, including on Antigravity and the other ACP engines.
"Keep an eye on my day" is on by default once apps are connected; pause or delete the routine to turn it off.
Bots find the right tool faster when many apps are connected.
In a group chat, a bot keeps each room's facts to that room.
Teammate bots no longer get stuck re-sending work they already sent.
A sleeping dusk cloud wakes more reliably.
A new bot says hi with what's on your plate instead of asking what you'd like.
Android app 1.2.12 is in this release; it registers for push notifications as soon as it pairs.
Routines can follow each other: one can read another's latest report, or run as soon as the one it follows finishes.
A script-only routine runs a command on its schedule and posts what it prints, with no AI turn.
A routine can set how late a missed run may still start, including never.
A self-hosted server can tell time in its owner's time zone (DUSK_ADOPT_TIME_ZONE=1), like a dusk cloud.
A bot can mark its own routine run as failed when the data it needs is broken.
Script checks on a server installed without install.sh explain the AppArmor fix instead of asking for a reinstall.
A script check that wakes the AI uses the routine's own time limit, not a fixed 60 seconds.
When a chat engine runs out of credit, rate-limits or goes down, the turn carries on with the bot's next engine.
Bots can read each other's chats, read only, on by default; turn it off under Permissions.
A reply carries the full message it replies to.
Phone pairing works with servers linked through the second link node.
Quitting on a Mac no longer hangs on a blank window when the direct link to a server fails.
A message you send a bot from Telegram or Discord no longer turns that thread into the bot's main chat.
Cmd+= (Ctrl+= on Windows and Linux) makes text bigger, beside Cmd+- and Cmd+0.
The Mac app no longer waits for its rollout turn when its own server already runs the newer version.
Long chats with many hidden tool steps no longer bounce on "Show later messages".
Antigravity's added Google accounts start Google sign-in and never show Claude's sign-in.
Long chats open and scroll back faster, and the app downloads less on first load.
A follow-up typed while the server is unreachable stays on screen and sends once it is back.
Lists and quotes carry on while you type in the message box.
Android: notifications through a Messages channel, the microphone for voice, and plain http only to local addresses.
Smoother motion when opening and leaving a chat on the phone.
